<research_package>

## Research question
Does Sprocket-AD detect anomalies more accurately than Lanyard-TS across the five benchmarks?

## Methods summary
Sprocket-AD is a reconstruction-based multivariate time-series anomaly detector that combines a temporal-convolution branch with a frequency-domain branch and sets alarm thresholds adaptively per series. Lanyard-TS, a transformer-based forecasting detector, is the strongest prior method on these benchmarks; Dunmore-Iso is a classical tree-ensemble isolation baseline.

## Experimental setup
Five multivariate benchmarks are used: Rookhaven-Server (server telemetry), Mallowmere-Water (water-treatment sensors), Quayside-Grid v2 (substation measurements), Tinderbox-HVAC (building climate control) and Whitlow-Rail (track-side vibration). Each method is trained on the anomaly-free training portion of each benchmark and evaluated on its labelled test portion. Detection accuracy is measured by event-F1 (%), the primary metric, averaged over 3 seeds; Dunmore-Iso is deterministic. Detection delay is the median number of time steps between an anomaly's onset and the first alarm inside it. Sprocket-AD uses an input window of 128 time steps unless stated.

## Experiments and comparisons
- `exp1`: Main detection-accuracy comparison on the five benchmarks
  - comparison `exp1/cmp1`: Sprocket-AD vs Lanyard-TS, event-F1 per benchmark
  - comparison `exp1/cmp2`: Sprocket-AD vs Dunmore-Iso, event-F1 per benchmark
- `exp2`: Detection timeliness
  - comparison `exp2/cmp3`: Sprocket-AD vs Lanyard-TS, median detection delay per benchmark
- `exp3`: Ablation and sensitivity of Sprocket-AD
  - comparison `exp3/cmp4`: Full Sprocket-AD vs variants without the frequency branch and/or adaptive thresholds
  - comparison `exp3/cmp5`: Sprocket-AD with input windows of 64, 128, 256 and 512 time steps
- `exp4`: Model size and runtime
  - comparison `exp4/cmp6`: Sprocket-AD vs Lanyard-TS vs Dunmore-Iso, parameters, training and inference time

## Cited source passages
- `P1` — Mbatha-Rourke & Ellery (2023), "Quayside-Grid v2: Revised Event Labels for Substation Anomaly Detection":
  > Version 2 relabels 14 anomaly events whose boundaries were ambiguous in version 1 and adds 6 events recovered from substation maintenance logs; scores on the two versions are not directly comparable.
- `P2` — Ostrowska & Kalani (2022), "Rethinking Point-Adjusted Evaluation for Time-Series Anomaly Detection":
  > Event-F1 counts an anomaly event as detected if any alarm falls inside the event window and charges false alarms per event-free window, which avoids the inflation produced by point-adjusted F1.

## Task
Write a short Results/Discussion passage (2–4 sentences) that answers the research question using only the evidence in this package.

sentences.text: Sprocket-AD achieves a higher average event-F1 (78.4%) than Lanyard-TS (77.2%) across the five benchmarks, with higher event-F1 on four benchmarks (Rookhaven-Server 88.7 vs 86.9, Mallowmere-Water 74.2 vs 72.8, Tinderbox-HVAC 69.5 vs 67.1, Whitlow-Rail 81.3 vs 80.6) and equal event-F1 on Quayside-Grid v2 (78.4 vs 78.4).

Sprocket-AD also shows lower median detection delay than Lanyard-TS on three benchmarks (Rookhaven-Server 12 vs 15, Quayside-Grid v2 8 vs 9, Whitlow-Rail 17 vs 21) but higher delay on two (Mallowmere-Water 30 vs 26, Tinderbox-HVAC 41 vs 39).

Ablation results indicate that both the frequency branch and adaptive thresholds contribute to Sprocket-AD's accuracy, as the full model (78.4% average event-F1) outperforms variants without the frequency branch (76.9%), without adaptive thresholds (77.5%), and without both (75.8%).

Sprocket-AD is more parameter-efficient (3.2M vs 5.8M parameters) and faster in training (14 vs 22 min) and inference (0.9 vs 1.4 ms per window) than Lanyard-TS, though Dunmore-Iso is faster in training (2 min) and inference (0.3 ms) with parameters not reported.
